:::{#def-absolutely-integrable}
#### Absolutely integrable function

Let $(S, \salg, \mu)$ be a [measure space](#def-measure-space).
A [measurable](#def-measurable-function) function $f : S \to \reals$
is **absolutely integrable** with respect to $\mu$
(often just called **integrable**)
if the integral of its [absolute value](algebra.qmd#def-absolute-value) is finite:

$$\int_S \abs{f} \, d\mu < \infty$$

The property itself is called **absolute integrability**.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-absolutely-integrable-integral}
#### An absolutely integrable function has a finite integral

If $f$ is absolutely integrable,
then $\int_S f^{+} \, d\mu$ and $\int_S f^{-} \, d\mu$ are both finite,
because $f^{+} \le \abs{f}$ and $f^{-} \le \abs{f}$,
so each sum in @def-integral-nonneg for $f^{+}$ or $f^{-}$
is at most the matching sum for $\abs{f}$.
So $\int_S f \, d\mu$ (@def-integral) is a real number.

:::
